text: The Yoneda lemma states that for a locally small category C, an object A, and a functor F: C → Set, there is a bijection:
choices: Hom(A, B) ≅ Hom(B, A) for all B
Nat(Hom(A, −), F) ≅ F(A), natural in A and F
Nat(F, G) ≅ Hom(F, G) for all functors F, G
explanation: Yoneda gives Nat(Hom(A,−), F) ≅ F(A), the bijection sending a natural transformation α to α_A(id_A); everything is forced by where id_A goes. Its embedding corollary — A ≅ B iff Hom(−,A) ≅ Hom(−,B) — says an object is determined by its morphisms to all others. The other options are not the lemma.
